title: Good Leaders Are Easy to Please But Hard to Satisfy
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Admired Leadership offers a maxim for leaders: be easy to please but hard to satisfy. The post warns that high standards can harden into withholding praise, focusing on the negative and valuing standards over the people who meet them. The corrective is that leaders can reinforce small efforts in the moment without lowering what counts as quality in the end result. Appreciation of everyday acts is paired with a continuing push for improvement. The author claims this balance creates a dynamic climate where people feel appreciated yet know they must keep striving, and recommends adding the maxim to a leader's mental canon.
points: High standards often lead leaders to withhold praise and fixate on the negative, creating a hard edge.
Being hard to satisfy does not require a shortage of compliments.
Easy to please means praising small acts and everyday effort in the moment.
Excellence remains the gold standard that never becomes less important.
The balance of appreciation and continuous improvement motivates people to produce their best work.
quotes: Good leaders have high standards, expect others to attend to the finest details, just as they do, and don’t declare excellence very easily. Unfortunately, for some leaders, this means they withhold praise and encouragement and focus much more on the negative than the positive.
Over time, they create a hard edge where quality and standards matter more than the people who produce them.

The best leaders have learned they can hold the highest of standards and expectations while also supporting and encouraging those around them every day. Being hard to satisfy doesn’t require a shortage of praise and compliments.
Easy to please” simply means that good leaders can reinforce the positive in the moment without compromising what counts as quality in the end product or outcome.
Leaders who are appreciative of small acts and everyday efforts are viewed as easy to please. They find simple acts and minor accomplishments worthy of comment and praise.
People feel appreciated but know they must continue to strive for more. That’s the reality the best leaders most want to create.
